articles.title: Abhishek Sharma on the cusp of T20I history, 53 runs away from breaking Suryakumar Yadav’s unique record
articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma could turn Friday's second T20I against the West Indies into another landmark night in his rapidly evolving international career.
articles.body: Abhishek Sharma could turn Friday's second T20I against the West Indies into another landmark night in his rapidly evolving international career. The India opener needs just 53 runs to complete 2,000 T20I runs, but the milestone itself is only half the story.If Abhishek gets there quickly enough, he could take down a record currently held by none other than his former captain and one of the most explosive batters in T20 cricket, Suryakumar Yadav.SKY's 1,164-ball record in sightSuryakumar holds the world record for reaching 2,000 T20I runs in the fewest balls. He reached the landmark in 1,164 deliveries, surpassing Australia's Aaron Finch, who had taken 1,283 balls.Abhishek currently has 1,947 runs from 997 balls. That means he has 167 balls as a theoretical maximum to score the 53 runs and equal SKY's 1,164-ball mark.But if he wants to break the record, he must get to 2,000 in 1,163 balls or fewer, meaning he has to score those 53 runs within his next 166 balls.A record tailor-made for Abhishek's approachAbhishek has built his reputation around an attacking brand of T20 cricket. His current T20I career strike rate stands at a staggering 195.29, with 1,947 runs coming from just 997 deliveries. He has also already smashed 135 sixes and three centuries in the format.The left-hander has shown just how quickly he can change a game. Earlier this year, he smashed a T20I century in only 30 balls against Afghanistan, the fastest century by an Indian in the format.So while 53 runs may sound like a modest target, the real question on Friday will be: how quickly can he get there?West Indies stand in the wayAbhishek made a brisk start in the series opener in Lucknow, scoring 21 off 10 balls before Roston Chase dismissed him. India went on to win by eight wickets, with Shreyas Iyer smashing an unbeaten 102 off 43 balls to give the hosts a 1-0 lead.Now, with Ranchi hosting the second T20I, Abhishek has the chance to turn a personal milestone into a piece of T20I history.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Tell your story': Pat Cummins' blunt response to Usman Khawaja's book on Sandpapergate
articles.summary: Australia captain Pat Cummins has played down concerns that Usman Khawaja’s upcoming autobiography could bring fresh attention to the 2018 ball-tampering
articles.body: Australia captain Pat Cummins has played down concerns that Usman Khawaja’s upcoming autobiography could bring fresh attention to the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, also known as Sandpapergate.Australia are returning to South Africa for the first time since the scandal. The three-Test series begins at Kingsmead on Friday, but Cummins said the incident had already been dealt with and the team had moved on.Cummins says the team has moved onCummins was part of the Australian bowling attack during the Test against South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018. Australia were caught using sandpaper to rough up one side of the ball illegally to generate more swing.The scandal created a major crisis for Cricket Australia. Captain Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, who was caught with sandpaper in his pocket, were banned for their roles in the incident.Cummins and fellow bowlers Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon denied knowing about the ball-tampering.All four are now back in South Africa for the three-Test series.Cummins confirmed that he had spoken to Khawaja, who was also part of the Australian team during the 2018 Test at Newlands. However, he said they did not discuss the matter in detail.“Didn't go back into too much detail. He just basically gave me the heads-up that he's doing a book, and yeah, as always, no worries. Tell your story. It's fine,” Cummins said.Khawaja’s book could revisit the scandalAustralian media reports have said that Khawaja had wanted the entire team to accept collective responsibility after the scandal. However, the suggestion was reportedly rejected at the time.Cummins said he did not know what Khawaja had written in his autobiography, which is due to be published next month.“You need to ask him,” he said. “It’s obviously a long time ago. All the investigations, everything was done back then. Answered every question a million times. So, yeah, it was dealt with then. Now all I can say is, as a group, we moved on, very happy with the last eight years, how we’ve been as a group and evolved.”Broadcaster takes a dig at AustraliaSouth African broadcaster SuperSport, whose cameras captured the ball-tampering incident in 2018, has also brought the episode back into focus.The broadcaster shared a social media clip showing Bancroft using sandpaper on the ball and the Australian team’s reaction after the players were caught.SuperSport added a warning ahead of the upcoming series, saying: “Our cameras will be sharp for this 3-match test series.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'There is pressure': Sahibzada Farhan on replacing Salman Ali Agha as Pakistan's T20I captain
articles.summary: Sahibzada Farhan is set to begin his stint as Pakistan's T20I captain when the team takes on Sri Lanka in the opening match of the three-game series in
articles.body: Sahibzada Farhan is set to begin his stint as Pakistan's T20I captain when the team takes on Sri Lanka in the opening match of the three-game series in Rawalpindi on Friday.Farhan has replaced Salman Ali Agha, who captained Pakistan at the 2026 T20 World Cup but has been left out of the 15-member squad.“It is an honour to captain Pakistan for the first time in a home series. I am very much excited for this new challenge,” Farhan said while speaking to the media on the eve of the first T20I.He admitted that captaincy brings pressure but believes his experience of leading teams in domestic cricket will help him handle the role.“Obviously, there is pressure of captaincy because you are leading the side and you have to show a different mindset,” he said. “I have captained previously in domestic cricket, so I have an idea of leading the side.”‘My father always prayed for this’Farhan said becoming Pakistan captain was something he had never expected. He also spoke about his father's wish to see him lead the national team one day.“I never imagined myself as Pakistan captain,” he said.Recalling his father's prayers, Farhan added: “Parents’ prayers really do come true.”The new captain believes he must lead from the front and perform well with the bat to set an example for his teammates. He also expressed confidence in his batting and said he hoped fans would enjoy his style of leadership.Farhan said he trusted the players selected for the series and expected the senior members of the team to help him on the field.“I have complete confidence in the players selected in the current squad. The presence of senior players will greatly assist me on the field,” he said.Farhan wants Pakistan to play attacking T20 cricketFarhan made it clear that he wants Pakistan to follow an attacking approach in the shortest format. He believes the team's top order has players who can support this plan.“We want to imply a T20 mindset. If you see our top order, which includes Fakhar Zaman, Maaz Sadaqat and Hasan Nawaz, they have a similar playing style to mine. I have got the team I wanted,” he said.The Pakistan captain also spoke about Sarfaraz Ahmed's influence on him as a leader.“I have played a lot under Sarfaraz Ahmed’s captaincy, and I really liked his leadership,” he said.Farhan also backed former Pakistan captains Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan, saying both remain capable of returning to T20 cricket.“Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan are the best players in the world. Both can return to T20 cricket at any time,” he said.Pakistan face Sri Lanka in three-match seriesPakistan will begin their three-match T20I series against Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Friday. The other two matches are scheduled for October 11 and 13. All three games will start at 6 pm, with the toss at 5:30 pm.The series trophy was unveiled in Islamabad on Thursday, with Farhan and Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis attending the ceremony. The series also marks the 250th international cricket match between the two countries.Pakistan head into the contest after winning a silver medal in the men's cricket competition at the Asian Games. The team trained for three hours in Rawalpindi on Wednesday and were scheduled to hold another session on Thursday.The 15-member squad includes uncapped players Razaullah and Mohammad Imran Randhawa. Fast bowler Naseem Shah is also in line to return to T20I cricket after last playing against Sri Lanka in February.Pakistan have several bowling options, with Abrar Ahmed leading the spin attack alongside Shadab Khan, Sufiyan Moqim and Arafat Minhas. Saim Ayub can also contribute with his off-spin. Naseem will lead the pace attack, which also includes Mohammad Salman Mirza, Razaullah and Randhawa.Khawaja Mohammad Nafay is expected to keep wickets, while Fakhar Zaman's return adds experience and attacking ability to the batting line-up. Maaz Sadaqat, Farhan, Hasan Nawaz and Abdul Samad provide further options with the bat.Pakistan have won 18 of their 31 T20I matches against Sri Lanka, while Sri Lanka have won 13. However, Sri Lanka swept their last bilateral T20I series in Pakistan 3-0 in Lahore in 2019.Mendis said his team were determined to put up a strong fight and improve their record against Pakistan.Pakistan vs Sri Lanka: T20I squadsPakistan: Sahibzada Farhan (captain), Abdul Samad, Abrar Ahmed, Arafat Minhas, Fakhar Zaman, Hasan Nawaz, M Imran Randhawa, Khawaja Nafay (wicketkeeper), Maaz Sadaqat, Naseem Shah, Razaullah, Saim Ayub, M Salman Mirza, Shadab Khan, Sufiyan Moqim.Sri Lanka: Kusal Mendis (captain), Kamil Mishara, Sineth Jayawardena, Lahiru Udara, Sahan Arachchige, Kamindu Mendis, Dasun Shanaka, Chamindu Wickramasinghe, Dunith Wellalage, Maheesh Theekshana, Vijayakanth Viyaskanth, Dushmantha Chameera, Binura Fernando, Nuwan Thushara, Eshan Malinga.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: BCCI Centre of Excellence treated 32 top cricketers last year
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Indian cricket board’s (BCCI) injury management programme at its Centre of Excellence (CoE) has been under renewed focus over the past 20
articles.body: New Delhi: The Indian cricket board’s (BCCI) injury management programme at its Centre of Excellence (CoE) has been under renewed focus over the past 20 months. Now, according to the CoE annual report, accessed by TOI, as many as 32 top men’s team players, including 20 BCCI centrally contracted players and 12 players under a new targeted/India ‘A’ category, underwent rehabilitation for injuries between April 2025 and March 2026. The list has swelled post IPL 2026, with at least two players breaking down in each series.Interestingly, the report states that the BCCI increased the CoE’s budget by nearly Rs 35 crore compared to the actual expenses in the previous financial year. The CoE’s expenses include administrative costs, courses and match expenses.The CoE’s projected expenses for 2026-27 now stand at Rs 127 crore, compared to Rs 92 crore in actual expenses last year.India’s Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill and head coach Gautam Gambhir have been vocal about how difficult it has become to plan tours because of a surge in injuries over the last year. While the report does not specify how many times each player reported to the CoE, it mentions that injuries to 68 players across genders were treated and managed by the BCCI-CoE Sports Science Medicine (SSM) team.When it comes to the nature of the injuries, the majority were soft-tissue injuries. The only impact injury treatment mentioned was that of Rishabh Pant, who underwent treatment following a foot fracture sustained during a Test in Manchester in July 2025.Interestingly, the report also reveals that Rohit Sharma underwent rehabilitation at the CoE during this period, but the BCCI never made an official statement about it. Rohit last reported to the CoE for a hamstring injury following this year’s IPL.The latest Team India players added to the list up to Sept 30 this year are Virat Kohli, Varun Chakravarthy, Prince Yadav and Harsh Dubey, besides multiple ‘targeted’ players. From that list, Jasprit Bumrah, Washington Sundar, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Harshit Rana, Hardik Pandya and Prasidh Krishna have been repeat cases. Rana, Pandya and Reddy have each spent at least four months at the CoE in the last 18 months.No SSM head, lack of coordination with Team IndiaThe BCCI advertised the post of SSM head at the CoE only last month. The post has been lying vacant since Nitin Patel resigned in March 2025.TOI understands that there has been a breakdown in communication between Team India’s SSM team and the CoE’s SSM team, with cricket head VVS Laxman being the only medium of communication. It has been learnt that Team India strength and conditioning (S&C) coach Adrian Le Roux suggested a few tweaks to workload management routines in June 2025, while the CoE has been reluctant to deviate from its own mechanisms.Personnel from the CoE’s SSM team travelled to domestic tournaments to monitor key India players under the injury prevention and management programme.The last time Indian cricket saw a spate of soft-tissue injuries was in 2021-22, when players suddenly moved out of playing in bubbles during the Covid-19 pandemic. That time, the issue was brought under control in two to three months. In 2017, too, there was a three-month phase when multiple players broke down after S&C coach Shanker Basu introduced drastic changes to the fitness programme.Fifteen budgeted camps didn’t happenAccording to the report, 15 of the 57 budgeted camps and tournaments were not conducted in the last audited year.The CoE conducted 25 elite/high-performance camps across age groups and genders, besides special camps for the north-eastern states. It also organised multiple courses and camps for S&C coaches, other coaches and match officials.Thirty-seven top men’s players opted for ‘training block’ programmeThe CoE started a programme called the ‘training block’ for contracted and targeted/India ‘A’ players. According to the report, 37 players, including 11 contracted players and 26 India ‘A’/targeted players, availed themselves of the programme, which focuses on strength and skill training.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s presence puts Sanju Samson under pressure ahead of 2nd T20I
articles.summary: Ranchi: Nearly four years after his last international appearance at the JSCA International Cricket Stadium, Ishan Kishan returns to familiar territory on
articles.body: Ranchi: Nearly four years after his last international appearance at the JSCA International Cricket Stadium, Ishan Kishan returns to familiar territory on Friday when India take on the West Indies in the second T20I, carrying the form and confidence of a player who has fought his way back into the Indian team.Ishan’s last international game here came in January 2023, when India lost a T20I to New Zealand. Much has changed since then. He subsequently lost his place in the India set-up, was dropped from the BCCI central contract list and then embarked on a comeback that has eventually seen him become an integral part of the national side.Now, with good form behind him and his home crowd in front of him, Kishan has a chance to turn his long-awaited return to Ranchi into a memorable one. The timing could hardly be better. India made a statement in the opening T20I, chasing down West Indies’ 172 in just 14 overs. Their aggressive approach left the visitors’ bowling attack with little room for error, and Kishan will be keen to make his own contribution as India look to take a 2-0 lead.India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak said the change of venue would not alter the team’s philosophy. “The way we are approaching the game, with a fearless approach and putting the team first, that’s the same way we will go,” Kotak said ahead of the game here on Thursday.Yet Ranchi could demand a little more adaptability than the opening game did.Though Kotak said on the eve of the match that “the pitch looked a good batting track”, the venue has not traditionally been a high-scoring T20 ground. In four T20Is here, the 200-run mark has never been breached, with India’s 196 for six against Sri Lanka in 2016 remaining the highest score. New Zealand have also successfully defended 176 at the venue.Rain and cool, cloudy conditions could add another variable, while dew may become important later in the evening. With temperatures expected to hover between 22°C and 24°C during match time, India could have to balance their attack carefully, particularly if they end up bowling second.That brings another selection question. Mayank Yadav was expensive in the opening game, leaving India to consider whether to persist with the express quick or bring fit-again Prince Yadav into the attack. They also have considerable spin depth, with Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav, Ravi Bishnoi and debutant Naman Dhir among the options. But if dew sets in, India’s spinners could find their task considerably harder.There is also a growing selection subplot in the batting department. The presence of teenage prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has increased the pressure on Sanju Samson, who has struggled for runs in his last four T20Is, scoring 11, 2, 7 and 9. With the teenager waiting in the wings, another low score could make the competition for the Kerala wicketkeeper-batter’s spot more interesting.West Indies, meanwhile, need a vastly improved bowling effort. Bowling coach Ravi Rampal admitted that his young attack, with most of its members having fewer than 15 or 20 T20I appearances, failed to maintain its execution for long enough in the opener.“It just boils down to the experience of the bowling group and then the execution of our plans. We weren’t good enough to execute for a longer period during the game,” Rampal said.That execution will be tested again by an Indian batting line-up that showed little hesitation in taking on the bowlers from the outset.But amid all the tactical questions, Ranchi’s biggest storyline remains Kishan. His journey back to India has already been significant. A substantial innings at the ground where his international journey briefly stalled would add another satisfying chapter to his comeback story.For Kishan, Friday is more than another T20I. It is a homecoming, and an opportunity to make it count.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘You can’t beat experience’: India coach explains Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return
articles.summary: Ranchi: VVS Laxman’s new role in India’s selection process and Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to the T20I squad point to the same priority: better
articles.body: Ranchi: VVS Laxman’s new role in India’s selection process and Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to the T20I squad point to the same priority: better communication and greater experience as India build beyond their current winning combination.Laxman, head of BCCI’s Centre of Excellence (CoE), will now attend every senior selection committee meeting, creating a direct link between the Bengaluru facility, the selectors and the Indian team management. The move is intended to ensure that information on players undergoing rehabilitation, particularly their fitness status, reaches the selectors directly.For the Indian team, though, the significance of the change is still evolving.“Honestly, I don’t know. I also came to know what you just said,” batting coach Sitanshu Kotak said when asked about Laxman’s new role during the pre-match press conference here on Thursday.Kotak did point to an existing line of communication between the team and Laxman, saying: “(Head coach) Gautam (Gambhir) always speaks to Laxman. That is the normal procedure, which I have always seen.”The broader selection strategy is already visible in India’s decision to bring Bhuvneshwar back into the T20I squad for the New Zealand tour after a four-year absence. The 36-year-old’s recall, following two strong IPL seasons, represents a conscious move towards experience in an attack otherwise populated by younger fast bowlers.Kotak said Jasprit Bumrah’s absence during parts of India’s recent schedule had highlighted the value of having an experienced bowler around the younger group. “We all know that you can’t beat experience. The youngsters are also performing well and getting selected, but at some stage you also need some experience,” he said.New Zealand’s conditions also appear to have influenced the thinking. Bhuvneshwar’s experience and ability to move the new ball give India another option as they prepare for the five-match T20I series. But the larger challenge remains balancing continuity with experimentation. India have rested Bumrah and other senior players in some games while giving younger players opportunities, even as the team continues to win.“There is a very thin line between keeping that balance,” Kotak said.The logic behind rotation is simple: India need to know whether their reserves can handle international cricket before they are forced to rely on them.“Any team in the world will require bench strength. And at some point you have to give them opportunities,” Kotak said.There can be a cost to that approach. “Sometimes results do suffer,” he admitted, although India’s depth has allowed them to experiment without significantly compromising results.That makes Laxman’s new role more than an administrative adjustment and Bhuvneshwar’s recall more than a nostalgic comeback. Both reflect a management group increasingly attentive to the finer details of squad-building, knowing when to back the established core, when to test the next generation and when experience can make the difference.India may be winning while experimenting. The next challenge is ensuring that experimentation strengthens, rather than disrupts, the winning formula.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Our cameras will be sharp': South African broadcaster SuperSport takes a dig at Australia over Sandpapergate ahead of Test series
articles.summary: South African sports broadcaster SuperSport has taken a dig at Australia ahead of their first Test series in South Africa since the 2018 ball-tampering
articles.body: South African sports broadcaster SuperSport has taken a dig at Australia ahead of their first Test series in South Africa since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, also known as Sandpapergate. Australia will face South Africa in a three-match series, with the opening Test scheduled at Kingsmead in Durban on Friday, October 9, at 1 pm IST.SuperSport posted a promo on X ahead of the three-Test series, saying its cameras “will be sharp”. The post included a camera emoji, bringing back memories of the incident at Newlands in Cape Town in 2018.SuperSport's cameras caught Bancroft in 2018SuperSport's reference goes back to March 24, 2018, when its cameras caught Australian batter Cameron Bancroft working on the ball with a small yellow object during a Test against South Africa at Newlands.The footage showed Bancroft using the object on the ball before putting it down his trousers. The incident led to the ball-tampering scandal that came to be known as Sandpapergate.The footage was shown on the big screen at the ground. Australia's then head coach Darren Lehmann sent a message to 12th man Peter Handscomb, while the incident quickly became a major talking point in cricket.SuperSport's cameras had also been asked to look out for anything unusual during the series after the umpires reportedly became suspicious about Australia's efforts to alter the ball.The broadcaster's coverage included more than 30 cameras, with 18 operated by camera crews.Several Australia players return with memories of 2018Australia's current squad includes several players who were part of the team during the Newlands scandal.Steve Smith, who was Australia's captain at the time, is now vice-captain under Pat Cummins. Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon also played at Newlands in 2018. Matthew Renshaw, who joined the squad as a replacement for the final Test of that series, is also back in the team. David Warner has retired, while Cameron Bancroft has not played a Test for more than six years.The scandal has received more attention in the Australian media than in South Africa in recent weeks. However, the team could still face some reminders of the incident during the tour.Australia return to Newlands for the third TestSouth Africa enter the series as reigning World Test Championship winners after beating Australia in last year's final at Lord's. Australia, meanwhile, will look to collect points in the 2025-27 World Test Championship cycle. The second Test will be played in Gqeberha from October 18.The third Test, scheduled to begin at Newlands on October 27, will bring Australia back to the venue where the 2018 scandal unfolded.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India rivals, Indian roots: The stories of Australia ‘A’ stars Nikhil Chaudhary and Tanveer Sangha
articles.summary: Puducherry: India are Australia’s biggest on-field rivals.
articles.body: Puducherry: India are Australia’s biggest on-field rivals. But these days, the Aussies are banking heavily on Indian-origin players who are making a mark at the highest level. As Australia ‘A’ continue their tour of India, two Indian-origin players brought up in different environments, Nikhil Chaudhary and Tanveer Sangha, offer fascinating stories of migration, identity, perseverance and ambition.For Nikhil, Australia was never part of the original plan. Born in Delhi and raised in Ludhiana, he was playing domestic cricket for Punjab when a holiday to Queensland during Covid-19 turned into a life-changing detour.“I was already playing for Punjab. But then I had to make that decision of going away from the family and starting a new journey,” Nikhil told TOI on the eve of Australia’s second ‘A’ one-dayer.The transition meant starting from scratch. He worked at a Mexican restaurant and drove as a courier to pay his bills before cricket began opening doors. The medium-pacer from Punjab eventually reinvented himself as a leg-spinning all-rounder and earned an Australia debut this year.“It’s just a different culture we have in India, where we just take everything for granted because of our mom and dad working hard for us. Here, I had to start from zero. If you are not hard-working and not able to struggle, then it’s not possible to actually play for Australia,” the hard-hitting middle-order batter said.His family in Ludhiana has remained his biggest support system, even though his father’s allegiance during an India-Australia contest remains firmly with the Men in Blue.“My dad still supports India. Just because I moved to Australia doesn’t mean he’s going to support Australia,” Nikhil said.Tanveer, on the other hand, never planned to become a cricketer. Born in Australia to Punjabi parents, he treated cricket as “a little more than a summer pastime”. Leg-spin entered his life around the age of 13 and, slowly, taking wickets began turning a hobby into a possible career.His parents’ journey, however, gave him a deeper appreciation of what it took to reach this level. His father, Joga, who played kabaddi in India and later in Australia, and his mother, Upneet, built their lives as migrants.“They’ve made huge sacrifices to get us here,” Tanveer said. “They’ve given me everything, the resources, their time, taking me everywhere to training and games.”Tanveer is also eyeing a return to the Australian side, with Adam Zampa currently firmly established as the first-choice leg-spinner. The youngster, however, sees Zampa’s presence as motivation rather than a roadblock.“My job is to keep getting better and hopefully take over his spot when he retires,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘It cannot happen’: Ex-India cricketer rules out Vaibhav Sooryavanshi replacing Sanju Samson
articles.summary: The questions around Sanju Samson's place in India's T20I side have resurfaced after the wicketkeeper-batter endured another modest outing in the series
articles.body: The questions around Sanju Samson's place in India's T20I side have resurfaced after the wicketkeeper-batter endured another modest outing in the series opener against the West Indies, but former India opener Aakash Chopra believes dropping him for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is not an option at this stage.Samson has managed scores of 11, 2, 7 and 9 in his last four T20I innings, including a five-over contest against Japan. The recent run has come after he struck back-to-back fifties in the T20I series against Afghanistan.However, Sooryavanshi's emergence has added another dimension to the selection debate. The teenage batter opened alongside Abhishek Sharma during the Asian Games, with Samson batting at No. 3. VVS Laxman was India's head coach for the tournament, with Gautam Gambhir occupied with the ODI team against the West Indies.For the ongoing series, India have returned to the opening combination of Samson and Abhishek, the pair that featured in the team's T20 World Cup-winning campaign. Samson, however, managed only nine in the first T20I against the West Indies in Lucknow.Chopra has backed the Kerala batter to retain his place, arguing that the team cannot keep questioning his position after every failure.Speaking in a video shared on his YouTube channel, 'Aakash Chopra,' the former India opener dismissed the prospect of Sooryavanshi replacing Samson for the second T20I."Since Bihar is in the neighborhood, there is talk of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Will there be a chance of him playing? No, it won't be there. You will have to agree that it cannot happen that he plays now, and if we start saying this about Sanju Samson after every match, then we are damned. How will you manage cricket then? Just don't go there," he said.Chopra also discussed the possibility of India bringing Nitish Kumar Reddy into the playing XI, admitting that he would like to see the all-rounder given a chance but was unsure whether the team management shared that view."I seriously think about Nitish Kumar Reddy for sure. However, I can't do that either after the first match. I wanted you to play Nitish from the start itself, because how will you prepare him? However, that's my thinking and might be your thinking as well, but the Indian team is not thinking like that," he observed.India head into the second T20I in Ranchi on Friday, October 9, with a 1-0 lead in the five-match series after securing an emphatic eight-wicket victory in Lucknow.For Samson, the immediate task is to turn his start into a substantial contribution and quieten the growing criticism. He was dropped after three failures during India's tour of the UK, having been named Player of the Tournament at the T20 World Cup.With Sooryavanshi continuing to attract attention, Samson will be keen to make the most of his opportunity. While Chopra has played down the prospect of an immediate change, the debate over India's opening combination is unlikely to disappear if the wicketkeeper-batter's struggles continue.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Bas lage rhna hai': Back in rhythm, Mukesh Kumar pushes for India comeback | EXCLUSIVE
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The last time Mukesh Kumar played for India, he claimed a four-wicket haul against Zimbabwe in Harare.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The last time Mukesh Kumar played for India, he claimed a four-wicket haul against Zimbabwe in Harare. Since then, he has been out of the national setup. More than two years later, the Bengal pacer is back on the selectors’ radar after being picked in the India A squad for the New Zealand tour.What can a cricketer do when they have played all three formats for India and are then suddenly left out in the cold? "Bas lage rhna hai (All we can do is keep pushing)," Mukesh tells TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interview.Mukesh, who will turn 33 in three days, is getting ready to play his sixth first-class game in less than two months. He picked up 12 wickets in East Zone's title triumph in the Duleep Trophy, then went on to play a county match for Nottinghamshire, before returning to pick up eight wickets in the Irani Cup, helping Rest of India lift the trophy. Now, from Sunday, he will be playing for Bengal against Delhi in their Ranji Trophy opener before taking a flight to New Zealand.The seamer, who struggled with a calf injury last season, admits he is at his best in terms of fitness and says he has found his rhythm.The longer I play through a season, the better my rhythm becomes. That did not happen last year because of the injury."As a rhythm bowler, I need to play regularly to get into my groove, particularly in red-ball cricket. The longer I play through a season, the better my rhythm becomes. That did not happen last year because of the injury," he said."I had an injury last year and did not get to play much. I played only three Ranji Trophy matches, two or three Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy matches and five Vijay Hazare Trophy matches. This year, however, I have already been part of teams that won the Duleep Trophy and the Irani Cup. I am enjoying my cricket, my body is getting into a rhythm, and I feel I have prepared well," he added.One thing Mukesh is enjoying most about this season is the way the ball is leaving his hand. What has worked well for him is his upright seam. He feels his wrist is firmly cocked at the point of delivery, and his slightly split fingers come down so straight that the seam invariably comes out bolt upright."My strength is my seam position. I am not someone who relies heavily on swing. Whatever the ball is, whether it is an SG, Duke or Kookaburra, I try to land it on the seam," he said."My rhythm was slightly off in the first innings (of the Duleep Trophy). I could not quite understand what was happening, although the pitch was offering plenty of assistance on the first day. Even when my rhythm was not at its best, I managed to trouble the batters. I started finding my rhythm towards the end of the first innings, and it carried into the second innings. Once that happened, you saw the difference."Mukesh also candidly admits that most of his wickets this season have come with the SG ball. Of the 22 wickets he has taken this season, 21 have come in India with the SG ball. He picked up a solitary wicket in the one county match he played for Nottinghamshire. Mukesh has experience of bowling in different conditions, but this time around, he is doing his homework before landing in New Zealand.Recently, I had a long chat with Mohammed Shami as well. He has shared his experience of bowling in New Zealand and has advised me on things I can do differently.In the Bengal team, he shares the dressing room with Mohammed Shami and Akash Deep, but he has also reached out to Sourav Ganguly."I have played in Australia, Bangladesh and South Africa, so I have experience of bowling in different conditions," he said."I speak to Ranadeb Bose most often. I also talk to Laxmi Ratan Shukla. Recently, I had a long chat with Mohammed Shami as well. He has shared his experience of bowling in New Zealand and has advised me on things I can do differently."I have also met Sourav sir. He was one of India's best captains. He has shared details about the conditions in New Zealand. I enjoyed exchanging ideas with him," said Mukesh.Mukesh knows he is not getting any younger. He has the skill set but for fast bowlers, that's not always enough. A three-point plan was drawn for the off-season and the hard yards are paying off."The first thing I worked a lot on was my fitness. I have also worked extensively on my line and length. Lastly, I have added a few yards to my pace. These were the three areas I focused on, and the improvement was visible in my bowling during the Duleep Trophy and Irani Cup," he said.Mukesh also talks about the insecurity that creeps into a fast bowler's mind when he gets injured, as rehabilitation can be a long and frustrating process. He also explains the changes a bowler needs to make to regain full fitness.At times, the mind can become frustrated when you are injured. Cricket is happening all over the world, and you are lying in bed, unable to play. You see other players representing India and wonder when you will return."A fast bowler has to be careful about his diet. You need to avoid too much oily and spicy food. Getting adequate sleep and maintaining good habits are key as well. Mental peace is another important aspect. If you keep worrying about things, you will not sleep properly and may end up staying awake all night. You need to eat well, sleep well, follow good habits and keep up with your rehabilitation. You must also follow the instructions of your trainers and physiotherapists."At times, the mind can become frustrated when you are injured. Cricket is happening all over the world, and you are lying in bed, unable to play. You see other players representing India and wonder when you will return. I am very grateful to God that I have such a supportive family. Whatever happens at home, my family ensures that it does not affect me. My mother, in particular, makes sure that I do not have to worry about anything. Now I have my wife as well, so that support system is important," he said.For fast bowlers, the packed cricket calendar leaves little room to breathe. The IPL is followed by state leagues and then a packed domestic season featuring tournaments such as the Duleep Trophy, Irani Cup and Ranji Trophy, along with the white-ball competitions. With matches coming thick and fast, managing workloads becomes crucial, particularly for bowlers whose bodies endure immense physical stress. Injuries can derail careers, making it essential to recognise the warning signs.So, how does a fast bowler know when he is pushing his body too far?"Body hamesha 80% hi rehta hai, 20% niggle toh rehta hi hai (A fast bowler can never be 100% fit. There will always be some niggle or the other)," he said with a laugh."Before an injury happens, the body gives you signals. It is almost as if God is telling you not to push yourself any further because something could go wrong. The body works in a similar way. If you push beyond your limits, you may end up getting injured. If you understand your body and recognise those warning signs, you can ease off and ask for rest when necessary. For example, if you feel tightness or stiffness, you should communicate that to the team management and explain that you might need a break from the next match. Ultimately, it also depends on what the management wants and how it assesses the situation."You have to recognise when your workload is becoming excessive. If there is a tight match, you naturally want to give everything you have. You feel that whatever happens afterwards can be dealt with later. But you cannot approach every match that way. You have to understand when your body needs rest. If you do not, you could end up paying a heavy price," he further explained.A workhorse in domestic cricket, Mukesh has earned recognition for his performances and is now back in contention for a place in the national setup. With a new challenge awaiting him in New Zealand, the Bengal pacer knows that every opportunity counts. After more than two years on the sidelines, he is determined to keep pushing and make his way back into the Indian dressing room.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Nic Maddinson creates unwanted record for longest duck by a Test opener in 21st century
articles.summary: Nic Maddinson’s return to Test cricket after nearly a decade got off to a disastrous start as the Australia opener endured a 33-ball duck against South
articles.body: Nic Maddinson’s return to Test cricket after nearly a decade got off to a disastrous start as the Australia opener endured a 33-ball duck against South Africa in the first Test at Kingsmead, Durban, on Friday.Maddinson’s 0 off 33 balls is the third-longest duck by an opener in Test history. It is also the longest innings for a duck by a Test opener in the 21st century, making it an unwanted milestone on his comeback to the national side.The 34-year-old was dismissed after Travis Head fell for nine, leaving Australia in early trouble after captain Pat Cummins won the toss and elected to bat on the opening day.Maddinson was drafted into the squad as a replacement for the injured Cameron Green, making a return to the Test set-up after overcoming testicular cancer. His previous Test appearance came during the 2016-17 home summer, when he managed just 27 runs across three matches.However, his recall had come under scrutiny even before the series began, with former Australia opener Matthew Hayden questioning the selectors’ decision to bring back a batter who had not played first-class cricket since early 2025.Speaking on the All Over Bar The Cricket podcast, Hayden launched a scathing attack on the selection panel and questioned the standard of players being picked for the national team.“Where we are at is that we are promoting the greatest pile of mediocrity that we’ve seen in a generation of cricket,” Hayden said.He also questioned the expectation that players with modest first-class averages could translate that form into success at the highest level, taking aim at chief selector George Bailey and Tony Dodemaide.“And if we continue to lay that out and expect that a bloke averaging 35 is going to average 55 in Test match cricket, George Bailey and Tony Dodemaide, you are dreaming. I will just put it that simply. You are frigging dreaming. And you are piling up this dog s*** explanation, and you are, in my opinion, disrespecting first-class cricket. Absolutely dead set you are. You should be picking guys that are averaging 45 or more, and you can’t, because they don’t want to play,” Hayden said.Maddinson’s first-class average of 37.11 had further fuelled the debate around his selection. Cummins, however, had backed the batter ahead of the series, saying he was settled in his game.With Head also dismissed cheaply, Australia faced an early test of their batting depth against a South African side that recalled Anrich Nortje and opted for two spinners. Kagiso Rabada was left out as he continues his recovery from a hamstring injury.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
